headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from shared-bus Pipecat feeding Superset; data leakage and capability conflict are limited by allowlisted egress and no shared write surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pipecat explicitly uses a shared bus and shared state across instances, so its outputs can be propagated into another component. Superset exposes an API and is a data-engineering system that may consume upstream content. The pairwise bridge is plausible, but no direct evidence shows permissive instruction parsing, so I choose medium rather than low due to the shared-bus default.
conditions: IF Pipecat output is forwarded onto the shared bus as text that Superset later interprets as instructions
IF Superset ingests upstream text without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a bus-level provenance tag and reject untrusted instruction-like payloads
Prefix all inter-agent messages with a fixed schema and strip free-form directives
Review one representative message path for prompt-like content
Disable any automatic action triggered by bus messages
requires-engineering: add content provenance enforcement between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pipecat touches audio, video, images, text, and conversation state, while Superset is a data-engineering tool with API access. Even though both only show allowlisted egress and no secrets/OAuth scopes, a shared bus can move sensitive conversational data into Superset outputs or dashboards. The shared data path is plausible in default deployments, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Pipecat conversation state or media is routed into Superset datasets or charts
IF Superset exports those datasets to users who should not see the original media/text
mitigations: Remove sensitive fields before publishing to Superset
Create a separate workspace for any Pipecat-derived dataset
Verify one dashboard for accidental inclusion of raw transcripts
Turn off automatic dataset refresh for Pipecat feeds
requires-engineering: implement field-level redaction before ingestion

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have allowlisted network egress, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git, database, or OAuth write scopes. Pipecat’s shared-bus concurrency could create coordination issues, yet Superset’s profile does not expose overlapping mutable write surfaces. With no shared write target documented, conflict risk stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external mutable resource
IF an orchestrator maps the shared bus to a shared writable backend
mitigations: Confirm the two agents do not share a writable directory
Assign separate service accounts for any external API use
Check one deployment manifest for overlapping write mounts
Serialize any shared-resource updates manually
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable backend

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can generate conversation content and analytics/metrics, and Superset can consume API-fed data for analytics. That creates a plausible path where Pipecat output becomes authoritative input to Superset without verification. No evidence shows Superset critically evaluates upstream content, so the default risk is a medium cascading error rather than low.
conditions: IF Pipecat-generated text or metrics are ingested into Superset as trusted facts
IF Superset dashboards or downstream actions are built from that unverified feed
mitigations: Add a human review step before publishing Pipecat-derived metrics
Label all upstream-generated fields as unverified in Superset
Sample one dashboard query for direct dependence on agent output
Disable any automation that acts on dashboard values
requires-engineering: add validation rules for upstream agent outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and show no secrets, OAuth scopes, or explicit residency/certification claims. The only concrete compliance concern is that Pipecat touches audio/video/text while Superset may store analytics derived from them, but no mismatch is documented. Because the evidence is sparse, I keep this low and avoid inventing residency or certification gaps.
conditions: IF regulated data from Pipecat is stored in Superset without a documented retention policy
IF either deployment is later assigned a residency or certification constraint not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Document the data class for every Pipecat-to-Superset feed
Set a short retention window on derived analytics
Review one export path for regulated fields
Add a deletion procedure for derived dashboards
requires-engineering: map residency and certification requirements before production use
